title: close, archive and demote relocate records too, but the completion staging hint is complete-only
description:
Found while implementing QCLI-311 (opum-ai/quest-cli#419) and filed rather than absorbed into that task. QCLI-221 makes status and on-disk location independent, and exactly four commands relocate a record: task complete, task close, task archive and task demote. The QCLI-311 slice added the human-surface staging hint to task complete only (completionStagingHint in src/cli/main.ts, gated on command === complete), while the task-finalization guide names the other three in a single sentence. So close, archive and demote still carry the commit-staging hazard QCLI-311 closed for complete, through the same composition: the move is left unstaged, and a repo-wide git add -A used to stage it also stages any unrelated tracked file merely missing from the working tree.

Ruled by opum-agent 2026-09-29 as EXECUTION, the same shape as QCLI-311 option 2: extend the human-surface hint to the other three relocating commands. Human text output only (plain and pretty); the JSON envelope stays unchanged.

Notes for whoever takes it:
1. Each command needs its OWN destination named, not a hardcoded one: complete and close move a record into .quest/completed/, archive moves it to the archive location, and demote moves it back toward tasks/. Derive the destination from the operation, and verify each by running the real commands in a disposable workspace the way QCLI-311 did, rather than asserting the behaviour from reading the code.
2. The forms to name are the scoped git add -A .quest/, or the record two paths; both were measured to stage a rename (git 2.55.0; see QCLI-311 implementation notes for the measurements).
3. Tests: extend test/qcli311-completion-staging-hint.test.ts or add a sibling; keep asserting the JSON envelope key order for every command touched.

Evidence: PR opum-ai/quest-cli#419; the guide section The commit that carries a completion in src/application/agents/guides.ts.

acceptanceCriteria.text: task close prints a staging hint naming the destination it actually used (.quest/completed/<id>.json), and its JSON envelope is byte-shape unchanged
task archive prints a staging hint naming .quest/archive/tasks/<id>.json, and its JSON envelope is unchanged
task demote names .quest/tasks/<id>.json when it relocated a record out of a retention location, and prints no relocation hint when the record was already stored at tasks; JSON envelope unchanged

Every destination is verified by running the real command in a disposable workspace, not asserted from the source; a test covers all four relocating commands and asserts the JSON envelope key order for each

plan: 1. Read the dispatch sites for close, archive and demote; derive each one destination from the operation rather than hardcoding it.
2. Generalize completionStagingHint to name the command and its destination; wire it into close, archive and demote alongside complete, human surface only (mode != json).
3. Verify each real destination by running the commands in a disposable workspace, the way QCLI-311 did, rather than asserting it from the code.
4. Extend test/qcli311-completion-staging-hint.test.ts (or a sibling); assert the JSON envelope key order is unchanged for every command touched.
5. Gates: bun run check and lore check.
6. Deliver per opum-sdlc; close in the PR.
implementationNotes:
ACs 1-4 evidence for QCLI-412. Every command below was RUN in a disposable workspace (git init + quest init + task create), not read off the source.

THE CHANGE. The destination is read from the mutation's own relocatedTo, set by TaskService.moveTask (complete, close, archive) and by demote lifecycle branch (back to tasks), rather than from a command-to-directory table in the CLI. Three destinations are involved, so a table -- or the hardcoded .quest/completed/ the QCLI-311 hint used -- would name the wrong path for archive and demote while looking correct for the two that share it.

AC1 (close): exit 0, stdout ends "Closed T-1: the record moved to .quest/completed/T-1.json. Stage the move ... git add -A .quest/ ...". File present at .quest/completed/T-1.json. JSON envelope keys still [schemaVersion, contractVersion, kind, data, principal].

AC2 (archive): exit 0, stdout ends "Archived T-1: the record moved to .quest/archive/tasks/T-1.json. ...". File present at .quest/archive/tasks/T-1.json. This is the case a hardcoded completed/ gets wrong; the test also asserts the output names archive/tasks and does NOT contain .quest/completed/. Envelope unchanged.

AC3 (demote, both shapes): from completed, exit 0 and "Demoted T-1: the record moved to .quest/tasks/T-1.json. ...", with .quest/completed/ empty afterwards -- the move really happened. From a record already at tasks (created + started, demoted --to "To Do"), exit 0 and NO hint at all: no "the record moved to" and no "git add" anywhere in stdout, because a same-location status write has no rename to stage. Envelope unchanged in both.

AC4: test/qcli412-staging-hint-relocating-commands.test.ts, 10 tests, each of the four commands covered in both plain and --json form, plus the no-hint case and the archive-not-completed case. Each plain assertion is paired with existsSync on the path the hint named, so a hint describing a move that did not happen fails.

MUTATION CONTROL, predicted before running and matched exactly. Replacing ${relocatedTo} with a hardcoded "completed" in relocationStagingHint reddens 3 of the 10 -- archive, demote, and the names-the-destination-not-the-usual-one case -- while complete, close and all four envelope assertions stay green. That split is the evidence the suite is not pinned to the implementation's identity, and it is also exactly how this defect would survive a complete/close-only test.

GATES: bun run check -- 1003 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. lore check -- exit 0, 63 files, 0 errors. quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude -- exit 0, state current.

ONE THING NOT ESTABLISHED, recorded rather than dropped. An earlier full-suite run of this same commit reported 1 failure: a test timed out after 5000ms (Bun's default), with 1002 pass. The re-run on an otherwise idle machine gave 1003 pass / 0 fail, and the failing test was not identified, because that run's output was truncated to its last lines. The plausible cause is resource contention I created -- two `bun run check` invocations were overlapping when it fired -- but that is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and I did not reproduce the flake deliberately. The 10 new tests all carry explicit 60_000ms timeouts, so the 5000ms default belongs to some other file. Not blocking: the suite is green on both the run cited and the final head.
finalSummary:
The staging hint now covers all four relocating commands. QCLI-311 added it to `task complete` only, but complete, close and archive all move a record out of .quest/tasks/ and demote moves one back, and each carries the same commit-staging hazard: an unstaged rename, where a repo-wide git add -A also stages unrelated deletions.

The destination is read from the mutation's own `relocatedTo` -- set by TaskService.moveTask and by demote's lifecycle branch -- rather than from a command-to-directory table in the CLI, because THREE destinations are involved: a table, or the hardcoded .quest/completed/ the hint previously used, would name the wrong path for archive and demote while looking entirely correct for the two that share it. demote is also conditional, relocating only when the record was stored outside tasks, so a demotion that stays put prints nothing -- no rename happened to stage.

VERIFIED (ACs 1-4) by RUNNING each real command in a disposable workspace, not by reading the source: complete and close name .quest/completed/<id>.json, archive names .quest/archive/tasks/<id>.json, demote names .quest/tasks/<id>.json with completed/ left empty afterwards, and a demote of a record already at tasks prints no hint at all. Every named path was checked against the file's actual location on disk, and the JSON envelope is asserted unchanged per command, including contractVersion at index 1 and principal last. Mutation control, predicted before running and matched exactly: hardcoding the destination back to completed/ reddens 3 of the 10 new tests -- archive, demote, and the names-what-it-used case -- while complete, close and all four envelope assertions stay green, which is precisely how this defect would survive a complete/close-only test.

The task-finalization guide sentence saying the three "relocate records the same way" is now precise about their differing destinations.

GATES: bun run check -- 1003 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. lore check -- exit 0, 63 files, 0 errors. quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude -- exit 0, state current.

DELIVERY: opum-ai/quest-cli#423. The source change at da947e8b is covered by Prepublication qualification run 36539775646 (push) and run 36539787373 (pull_request), both completed/success on that SHA, alongside Tracker integrity run 36539787364 and lore check run 36539787401.

ONE THING NOT ESTABLISHED, recorded rather than dropped: an earlier full-suite run of this commit reported 1 failure -- an unidentified test timing out at Bun's 5000ms default -- while two `bun run check` invocations were overlapping. The re-run on an idle machine gave 1003 pass / 0 fail and the flake did not reproduce. The overlap is a hypothesis, not a measurement; the implementation notes carry the detail.
